title: CO, CS, HCO, HCO<SUP>+</SUP>, C<SUB>2</SUB>H, and HCN in the diffuse interstellar medium
question: Discuss absorption lines of HCO+, C2H, HCN, CS, and HCO in the diffuse interstellar medium across a large sample of 88 sight lines and compare them with HCO+ and CO emission.

what.value: 21cm HI emission line profile integrals from the Leiden, Argentine, and Bonn (LAB) All-Sky HI survey

evidence.quote: HI column densities were derived from the Leiden, Argentine, and Bonn (LAB) All-Sky HI survey Kalberla et al.
Where we refer to optical reddening, the values cited were taken from the work of Schlegel et al. (1998).

what.value: PdBI absorption surveys of HCO+, C2H, HCN, and CS

evidence.quote: the rubric PdBI denotes results taken from the earlier surveys of HCO+ (Lucas & Liszt, 1996), C2H (Lucas & Liszt, 2000), HCN Liszt & Lucas (2001), and CS (Lucas & Liszt, 2002).

external_data.citation: Lucas & Liszt (1996); Lucas & Liszt (2000); Liszt & Lucas (2001); Lucas & Liszt (2002)

what.value: ALMA absorption data for 4 sight lines in the inner Galaxy

evidence.quote: In combination with ALMA observations of 4 sight lines at low latitude in the inner Galaxy (Gerin & Liszt, 2017; Liszt & Gerin, 2018)

what.value: ALMA HCO+ and CO absorption and DNM studies in Chamaeleon and the Galactic anticenter

evidence.quote: The rubric Chamaeleon refers to new data taken incidental to the DNM studies of Liszt et al. (2018, 2019)
New results incidental to DNM studies in the Galactic anticenter (Liszt & Gerin, 2023b) use the rubric Outer Galaxy.

what.value: Integrated HCO+ and CO emission profile results away from continuum background sources

evidence.quote: combining the new results with integrated profile results reported away from continuum background sources by Liszt (2020)

recipe.goal: Extract normalized absorption spectra and measure integrated optical depths and column densities
recipe.method: Extract spectral line profiles from the continuum-peak pixels of standard pipeline datacubes, normalize by the continuum flux in the respective spectral window continuum map, integrate optical depth over the HCO+ line span (or 3 km/s for non-detections), and apply linear conversion factors to derive column densities.
key_parameters: N(C2H) = 2.71 x 10^13 cm^-2 Y_CCH (with observed F=2-1 and F=1-0 components having 5/8 of total line strength)
assumptions: Permanent dipole moment of mu = 3.89 Debye for HCO+ and no collisional excitation above CMB
LTE hyperfine line strengths in 4:2:2:1 ratio for HCO

recipe.goal: Form pure emission spectra of HCO+, 12CO, and 13CO from IRAM 30m observations
recipe.method: Average four HCO+ emission spectra displaced by 1.2 HPBW (30'') in the four cardinal directions from the continuum source to avoid absorption contamination; average five positions (on-source and four displaced by 1 HPBW = 22'') for 12CO and 13CO on the main-beam antenna temperature scale.
key_parameters: Channel spacing 48.8 kHz (0.164 km s^-1) and spectral resolution 97.7 kHz (0.33 km s^-1) at 89.1885 GHz
assumptions: Emission displaced by 22''-30'' is representative of the gas along the continuum sight line

recipe.goal: Analyze Galactic-scale distributions and power-law abundance relations across the sample
recipe.method: Perform power-law linear regressions in log-log space of E_B-V, N(HI), N(H2), and W_CO against sin(|b|), and of molecular column densities against E_B-V, N(HCO+), and N(C2H).

recipe.goal: Decompose HCO+, HCN, and C2H absorption profiles into Gaussian kinematic components
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit all kinematic and hyperfine components by varying central optical depth, central velocity, and FWHM to minimize deviations from the observed line/continuum ratio exp(-tau), using HCO+ decomposition as an initial template for HCN and C2H, and match components across species.
key_parameters: Velocity matching criterion: separation in central velocity < 1/3 of the FWHM of the narrower component
assumptions: Hyperfine components of HCN and C2H have optical depth ratios proportional to their intrinsic LTE line strengths

recipe.goal: Compare HCO+ and CO in absorption and emission to derive excitation temperature, gas density, and X_CO
recipe.method: Interpolate ALMA absorption and IRAM 30m emission profiles onto common spectral grids for channel-by-channel comparison, and compare integrated profile quantities against weak-excitation radiative transfer models.
assumptions: Weak excitation limit (including electron collisions in diffuse gas with ionization fraction > 10^-4)

not_stated_but_needed: CASA and ALMA pipeline versions used to produce the standard pipeline datacubes and continuum maps
Exact rest frequency and transition of CS observed in the 87-98 GHz setup (presumably CS J=2-1 at ~97.98 GHz)
Exact conversion factor used to convert integrated HCO optical depth into N(HCO)
Software or optimization routine used for simultaneous Gaussian and hyperfine component fitting of the absorption spectra
Exact velocity integration windows used for each sight line to compute integrated optical depths
missing_for_reproduction: Individual Gaussian component fit parameters (velocities, FWHMs, optical depths) for each sight line are only summarized statistically, not tabulated per source.
Exact velocity integration intervals used to compute the integrated optical depths in Table B.1.
Tabulated values for the older PdBI/NOEMA and Inner Galaxy sight lines included in the 88-sight-line combined regressions (must be gathered from the cited companion papers).
Reduced IRAM 30m emission datacubes/spectra from project 003-19.
score_reason: The ALMA data reduction relies directly on standard archive pipeline cubes (peak-pixel extraction and continuum normalization), explicit conversion factors are given for HCO+, HCN, and C2H, and per-sight-line measurements are tabulated in Table B.1. However, exact velocity integration windows, the HCO optical depth conversion factor, and individual Gaussian component tables are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: All four ALMA project codes are public in the archive, the extraction from standard pipeline products is straightforward (continuum-peak pixel spectrum divided by continuum flux), and Table B.1 provides an exact numeric answer key for continuum fluxes and column densities across 46 sight lines.
